Over 10,000 homes are without water, reservoirs are drying up, a ghost village has emerged, wildfires are burning homes, and last month's wildfire tally broke records. In Stourbridge, West Midlands, wildfires have hospitalised three firefighters and a child, with PM Andy Burnham saying he is in touch with local leaders including West Midlands Mayor Richard Parker. A passenger train carrying 150 passengers has derailed near Lewes in East Sussex on what was the UK's fifth hottest day ever, injuring at least 18 people, two seriously; rails are believed to have buckled in the extreme heat. Experts warn Britain's railways are woefully behind in adapting to extreme weather. Southern Railway cancelled services until 10pm. British Transport Police, air ambulance, and rail crash investigators attended the scene. Wildfires are spreading across Europe, with 500 people evacuated in southwest France, hundreds of arson suspects arrested in France, and a Croatian holiday resort fire killing one person, injuring 40 and forcing 1,200 evacuations; blazes also hit Germany, Greece and Spain. Two people have died in wildfires on the Greek island of Salamis, with around 200 firefighters battling two blazes there. Belgium is fighting its biggest forest fire in more than a century near the German border, with 600 people evacuated and helicopters deployed. Across Europe more broadly, another day of near-record heat struck on Friday, though temperatures are expected to retreat to seasonal averages in the coming days.

clusters.state_of_play: Indonesia's twin earthquakes (7.7 and 6.4 magnitude) have killed at least 68 people, with thousands still awaiting aid and homeless on Flores Island days after the quake, overshadowing the country's Independence Day. Meanwhile Hurricane Lala weakened to a tropical storm after skirting Hawaii's Big Island without making direct landfall, avoiding the first direct hurricane hit on the island in over a century; it still lashed the island with hurricane-force gusts and nearly 3 feet of rain, causing flooding, at least one death, more than 100 homes damaged or lost, and over 180,000 households losing power, per Gov. Josh Green. The storm also struck Maui, stranding tourists, and officials issued a major disaster declaration. Meanwhile the same system fueled the worst Indiana flooding in over 30 years, killing at least six people—including a 4-year-old boy, two men, and three women—since storms began Aug. 11, per state homeland security spokesperson Liz Woods. Floodwaters peaked along Indianapolis's White River after Mayor Joe Hogsett ordered evacuations and crews conducted water rescues, with rain expected to ease in the capital region on Sunday though the National Weather Service warns flash flooding remains possible across central Indiana. Indiana's governor says the federal government has promised assistance, with more heavy rain expected across Indiana, Illinois and neighboring states this weekend.
